node.label: Richard Hofstadter
node.date_label: Social Darwinism in American Thought (1944) · The American Political Tradition (1948) · The Age of Reform (1955)
node.description: A historian of American political culture whose interpretations moved from economic-interest explanations toward ideas, status anxieties and political irrationality. Eric Foner’s retrospective distinguishes his critical account of consensus from celebratory consensus history and also identifies its limits.
node.representative_figures_and_works: Social Darwinism in American Thought (1944); The American Political Tradition (1948); The Age of Reform (1955).

incident_edges.relationship: Critically reworks the economic-conflict interpretation and explores ideological consensus in American politics.
incident_edges.evidence_note: Foner distinguishes Hofstadter’s critical consensus interpretation from celebratory versions and notes the later reconsideration of conflict.

incident_edges.relationship: Brings status anxiety, symbols and irrationality into accounts of political culture.
incident_edges.evidence_note: Foner’s named substantive reading also judges the treatment of Populists and Progressives exaggerated and elitist in important respects. This qualification survives the contribution arrow.

incident_edges.relationship: Hofstadter criticizes Turner’s weak critical response to expansion, Indigenous dispossession and anti-Mexican and anti-Chinese nativism, as quoted by Bogue (1994).
incident_edges.evidence_note: Bogue 206 and 220n 38 visually checked. His quotation identifies The Progressive Historians,104,106 in a 1969 manifestation. Hofstadter’s original chapter and 1949 essay remain unread; the claim is expressly mediated by Bogue.

incident_edges.relationship: Joint conception of the Oxford History of the United States provides a shared editorial project.
incident_edges.evidence_note: McPherson’s2000 recollection names both as conceiving a multiauthor series modelled on the Oxford History of England. Undirected editorial overlap, without causal priority or a shared interpretation of every subject. The transcript’s Hofstetter spelling is a variant, not a second historian.

incident_edges.relationship: As Foner recounts, defends the Populists’ corporate critique against Hofstadter’s emphasis on conspiracy and cultural hatreds.
incident_edges.evidence_note: Explicit named scholarly mediation: Foner’s2022 review, paragraphs beginning For decades and It was a book, distinguishes their disagreement from friendship. It also notes Woodward later conceded exaggerating white Populists’ racial egalitarianism. Original exchanges and complete books remain unread; editorial collaboration does not erase this disagreement.

records.context: Examines common assumptions through critical, selective portraits of political leaders; shared premises do not remove every conflict.

sources.title: Eric Foner, “Richard Hofstadter: Columbia’s Evolutionary Historian”, Columbia Magazine

verification.note: Complete substantive retrospective read. Foner was his student; discusses 1944, 1948, 1955 works, changing relation to Beard and consensus, intellectual influences and criticism of the Populist/Progressive interpretation. Hofstadter monographs unread.

verification.note: Complete published introduction v–xi, dated January 1948, title/imprint and contents read in local PDF text. Consulted Vintage reprint retains 1948 copyright but exact impression date is not established. Chapters unread. Shared assumptions coexist with conflict, critical portraits and a restricted selection of major-party leaders plus Phillips. Broad political/historical judgments remain attributed.
